per_request_costs.scrape: 1 credit / page (markdown, html, rawHtml all cost 1)
per_request_costs.extract: variable (~25-31 credits per MODO detail page measured this session)

firecrawl_pricing_2026.caching: cacheState: hit on scrape reuses prior result for ~4 hours at no additional savings (still 1 credit). Not a cost optimization, just a perf one.

slug_diff_incremental.content_hash_skip: Assume 80% of slugs unchanged day-over-day → 10 re-extracts × 28 = 280
slug_diff_incremental.plan_fit: HOBBY plan (3k credits/mo) INSUFFICIENT. STANDARD plan (100k) has 91k headroom. $83/mo.
slug_diff_incremental.note: Hobby only works if cadence drops to weekly (8.5k × 1/4 = ~2k/mo).

weekly_cadence_full.plan_fit: HOBBY plan (3k credits/mo) INSUFFICIENT at weekly full-refresh. Need Standard ($83/mo).

rawhtml_regex_days_approach.description: Use Firecrawl scrape with rawHtml format (1 credit), regex-extract valid_days from data-testid, feed the LLM ONLY fields that can't be regex'd (pct, tope, vigencia, min_spend, issuer_bank, variants).
rawhtml_regex_days_approach.projected_extract_cost: Unchanged (~28 credits) since LLM still reads the page. Savings come from ACCURACY, not cost. However, moving to server-side regex + direct GPT call (bypassing firecrawl_extract) could drop the ~25-30 credit surcharge entirely.

antibot_posture.anti_bot_fingerprints_in_rawHtml: NONE (no Akamai, Cloudflare challenge pages, PerimeterX, DataDome, Incapsula, Sucuri, hCaptcha, reCaptcha markers)
antibot_posture.cache_hit_rate: Firecrawl cacheState=hit on repeat scrapes (<4h apart) — server caches help performance, credits still charged per request
antibot_posture.raw_fetch_vs_firecrawl: Node raw fetch returns 47-char SPA shell (per Phase 1 PoC). Firecrawl's JS rendering is REQUIRED — this is an operational constraint.
antibot_posture.verdict: MODO has ZERO anti-bot protection on the public promo pages. They serve as marketing, not gated content. This is a sustainable scrape target for now. Risk: if they add WAF later, we'd need Firecrawl's stealth proxy (~2-5x credit cost).

breakthrough_finding_rawhtml_days.discovery: The rawHtml for MODO detail pages encodes the weekday active state via data-testid attribute:
breakthrough_finding_rawhtml_days.implication: valid_days can be extracted DETERMINISTICALLY via regex without LLM: match /data-testid="day-of-week-selected-([LMXJVSD])"/g and map letters to 0-6. This sidesteps the all-7-days LLM bug entirely.
breakthrough_finding_rawhtml_days.production_recommendation: Scrape with rawHtml format (1 credit), regex-extract valid_days first, then feed LLM the remaining content + the pre-computed valid_days as a hint. This gives 100% accuracy on valid_days at no extra cost.

competitor_signal_promoarg.findings: LinkedIn post (Dec 2025-ish, post_id=7442944621451816961) describes PromoArg as a personal project for centralizing bank promos. No 2026 posts specifically mentioning MODO scraper breakage, rate limits, or access issues surfaced in search.
competitor_signal_promoarg.note: LinkedIn blocks Firecrawl access to post content — only description snippet available. Deeper competitor investigation was not prioritized (time budget).
competitor_signal_promoarg.interpretation: No signal that MODO is actively blocking scrapers. PromoArg's own data suggests they rely on MODO as a source (same conclusion as our PoC).
